\title{The Shadow Price of Neutrality}
\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{\todo{author}}}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\begin{outline}{Abstract, 0.2 page}
\item Problem: a long/short pod under a platform's neutrality mandate at a fixed \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr risk budget $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}.
\item Approach: duals of the convex program at a root-found $\lambda^*$; three integer sensitivity estimators against certified secant intervals; big-M against perspective formulations $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:approach}.
\item Q1 finding: the liquidity cap, sector bounds and trading costs carry the cost; factor neutrality is nearly free for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$; at zero, sector and all-style neutrality cost about the same $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \ESectorMed, \SplitTradeMed, \CTwoSectorTight\ against \CTwoStyleTight, \IdealRetMomMin; Figs.~\ref{fig:costcurves}--\ref{fig:alignment}.
\item Q2 finding: the fixed-integer dual is exact when neither the support nor the active set changes within the step (max error \PredOneMax) and lies in $[L,H]$ in \ErrFixedInLH\ of \IOneBindTen\ binding cases; the best estimator depends on the step: at \IOneRobustDate\ ($n=\RobustN$) the fixed-integer dual is best at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ (\RobustFixedFive; perspective \RobustPerspFive, big-M \RobustBigMFive) and the perspective slope at \IOneDeltaPct\% (\RobustPerspTen\ against \RobustFixedTen; big-M \RobustBigMTen) $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:i1}.
\item Q3 finding: two mechanisms. The default-scaling root bound is consistent with Gurobi's outer approximation stopping early (\NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN; \NThreeGapDef\ against \NThreeGapMZero\ with a QCP node relaxation); the cone tolerance inflates incumbents (\ConeDefMax). The rescaled formulation (rows and cones rescaled together) removes both; presolve, not the formulation, closes big-M's gap $\rightarrow$ \RootRescBase, \RootDefBase, \PreBigMRootOn\ against \PreBigMRootOff; Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}.
\end{outline}
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
% drafted-by-chat (Claude, claude.ai chat, 2026-10-25) from the accepted proposal and this section's outline; Isaiah revises (Decision 62)
A multi-manager platform allocates capital to long/short equity teams, called pods. To keep one pod's risk from piling onto the others' books, it caps the pod's volatility (\RiskBudgetPct\%/yr here) and imposes a neutrality mandate on its dollar, beta, style and sector exposures. Every rule costs the pod expected alpha, and the platform reads each constraint's dual variable as that cost. In a convex program the dual is the derivative of the optimal value with respect to the bound wherever it is unique (A5), so the reading is exact. With a cardinality limit and a minimum position the program is mixed-integer, continuous duals carry no such guarantee, and a misread dual can lead the platform to loosen the wrong rule.

% drafted-by-chat
Clarke, de Silva and Thorley extend the fundamental law of active management with a transfer coefficient that measures how constraints dilute a forecast \cite{grinold2000active,clarke2002portfolio}, and Stubbs and Vandenbussche attribute a portfolio to its constraints through their duals \cite{stubbs2010constraint}. Lee and Stefek show that misaligned risk and alpha factors distort optimized portfolios \cite{lee2008risk}, and Ceria, Saxena and Stubbs frame such alignment problems \cite{ceria2012factor}; realistic shorts \cite{jacobs2005portfolio} and sparse portfolios \cite{bertsimas2022scalable} are related modeling work. Perspective cuts and reformulations strengthen mixed-integer programs with indicator variables, including portfolios with position thresholds \cite{frangioni2006perspective,gunluk2010perspective}. Geoffrion and Nauss survey postoptimality analysis for integer programs \cite{geoffrion1977parametric}, and Wolsey shows that integer duality needs price functions rather than prices \cite{wolsey1981integer}; the course texts give the background \cite{boyd2004convex,wolsey2020integer}.

% drafted-by-chat
This paper prices each constraint at equal risk, through the risk row's multiplier, and measures how far continuous sensitivity estimators drift once integrality enters. Q1 asks which constraints bind at a fixed risk budget and what each costs; Q2, how well continuous tools predict a constraint's true marginal cost under a cardinality limit and a minimum position; Q3, how big-M and perspective formulations compare and how solver tolerances interact with scaling (Sec.~\ref{sec:questions}). The contributions are:
(i) costs at equal risk by duality at $\lambda^*$, with the closed form $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ for the alpha kept under full factor neutrality (A1--A4): at least \IdealRetMomMin\ for momentum, while the liquidity cap carries the cost (median elasticity \ELiqMed);
(ii) certified secant intervals, of median relative width \WidthMed, that test the estimators against solver error (A8);
(iii) when the fixed-integer dual is exact: error at most \PredOneMax\ on a fixed support and active set, median \PredThreeMed\ when the support changes;
(iv) the perspective model's two scaling mechanisms, kept apart: a root bound consistent with outer approximation stopping early (\NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN\ instances) and a cone tolerance that inflates incumbents by up to \ConeDefMax\ of the objective, against \ConeRescMax\ when rows and cones are rescaled together (A9).
The project is a problem-formulation study on one universe, period and risk model; it is not a backtest and makes no performance claim.

\section{Problem Setting}
\label{sec:setting}

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Decision problem}
A \emph{pod}, one long/short equity team at a multi-manager platform, receives each month a forecast $\alpha_i$ of each stock's (\emph{name}'s) \emph{alpha}, its expected return beyond what its factor exposures explain, and chooses weights $w$ as fractions of AUM (assets under management, \$\AUMBillion B). The platform caps the \emph{ex-ante volatility}, the risk model's forecast $\sqrt{w\T\Sigma w}$ annualized, at \RiskBudgetPct\%/yr ($\sigma_m=\RiskBudgetPct\%/\sqrt{\MonthsPerYear}$ per month) and imposes a mandate that protects its other books. The \emph{factor exposure} is $y=B\T w$, $B$ the loadings on the market and five styles (size SMB, value HML, profitability RMW, investment CMA, momentum Mom); \emph{beta} is $y_{\mathrm{mkt}}$. \emph{Dollar}, \emph{beta}, style and \emph{sector neutrality} bound the net weight $|1\T w|$, $|y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|$, each $|y_k|$ and each $|S_j\T w|$, $S_j$ the 0/1 indicator of GICS sector $j$ (the standard industry classification; \NSectors\ sectors). \emph{Gross leverage} $1\T(w^++w^-)$ is the long plus the short weight. A stock's \emph{ADV} is its median daily dollar volume over \AdvWindow\ trading days; with the position cap $u$, the \emph{liquidity cap} (a fraction $\theta$ of ADV) gives $u_i=\min(u,\theta\,\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM})$. Shorts pay a \emph{borrow cost} $c$ per month (per year in Table~\ref{tab:mandate}) and trades a one-way \emph{trading cost} $\kappa$ (1~bp $=0.01\%$); from cash ($w_0=0$) trading costs $\kappa$ times gross. Table~\ref{tab:mandate} lists the base mandate.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Data and risk model}
Daily adjusted prices and volumes of the current S\&P~500 constituents (\PanelTickers\ tickers, \PanelStart\ to \PanelEnd) come from yfinance, sectors from the constituent list, and the daily Fama--French five factors, momentum and risk-free rate from the French library \cite{fama2015five,french_data_library,yfinance}. A day is valid for a stock with a return and a dollar volume of at least \$\ValidDollarVolumeM M; a stock is \emph{eligible} at a date if at least \ValidPct\% of the \RiskWindow\ trading days ending there are valid. At each of the \RiskMonthEnds\ month-ends (\RiskFirst\ to \RiskLast) eligible stocks' daily \emph{excess returns} (minus the risk-free rate) over that window are regressed on the six factors: $B$ holds the loadings, $D=\mathrm{diag}(d)$ the residual variances and $F$ the sample factor covariance, both scaled by \DaysPerMonth\ trading days to monthly, with $d$ floored at its \FloorPct th cross-sectional percentile, so $\Sigma=BFB\T+D\succ0$. The eligible universe has \UnivMin--\UnivMax\ names.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Alphas and alignment}
The momentum score, each stock's return over the \MomLookback\ trading days before the date skipping the last \MomSkip\ (it exists at \DisclosureDates\ of the \RiskMonthEnds\ month-ends), is z-scored across eligible stocks, winsorized at $\pm\WinsorClip$ and re-standardized; the alpha is $\alpha_i=\mathrm{IC}\cdot\omega_i z_i$ with information coefficient $\mathrm{IC}=\ICAssumed$ and residual volatility $\omega_i=\sqrt{d_i}$ \cite{grinold2000active}, an input signal (no backtest). A $D^{-1}$-weighted regression of an alpha $\alpha$ on the loadings splits it into a residual $\alpha_\perp=\alpha-B(B\T D^{-1}B)^{-1}B\T D^{-1}\alpha$ and a factor-spanned part $\alpha_\parallel=\alpha-\alpha_\perp$. The \emph{alignment share} $\varphi(\alpha)=\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha\in[0,1]$, on $\alpha$'s own, unrescaled split, is the factors' part of $\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$, the squared \emph{information ratio} (the best ratio of expected alpha to ex-ante risk); rescaling $\alpha$ leaves it unchanged. $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$'s $\alpha_\perp$ and $\alpha_\parallel$, each rescaled to $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$'s information ratio, also serve as signals. The \emph{transfer coefficient} $\mathrm{TC}=\alpha\T w/(\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}\sqrt{w\T\Sigma w})$ is the $\Sigma$-metric form of Clarke et al.'s \cite{clarke2002portfolio}.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The convex problem \prb}
The risk-budget problem \prb, with $w=w^+-w^-$, $w^\pm\ge0$, is
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\le\sigma_m^2,\quad y=B\T w,\\
& |1\T w|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{net}},\ |y_{\mathrm{mkt}}|\le\varepsilon_\beta,\ |y_k|\le b_k,\ |S_j\T w|\le h_j,\\
& 1\T(w^++w^-)\le G,\quad w_i^+,w_i^-\le u_i .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:prb}
\end{equation}
Since $c,\kappa>0$, at most one of $w_i^\pm$ is positive at an optimum. The optimal value $A^*$ is net expected alpha per month. Row $k$ has multiplier $\mu_k$; a parameter $p$ (a bound, $u$ or $\theta$) has the \emph{family dual} $\mu_p=dA^*/dp=\sum_k\mu_k\,\partial r_k/\partial p$ over the rows whose right-hand side $r_k$ moves with $p$ (A5): $\theta$ through every $\theta$-limited cap ($\partial u_i/\partial\theta=\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM}$), $u$ through every cap equal to $u$, a common sector or all-styles bound through all its rows. A \emph{key} is a parameter whose dual is reported: a family, or one sector's or style's row. The \emph{elasticity} $e_p=\mu_pp/A^*$ ($A^*>0$) is the percent change in alpha per percent change in $p$; a constraint \emph{binds} if $e_p\ge\BindTol$. The risk row's multiplier $\lambda^*$ is the price of risk at which a mean-variance investor picks the same portfolio (A1). A fixed risk budget, not a fixed $\lambda$, compares costs at equal risk: relaxing a constraint cannot buy alpha by levering up.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{The integer problem \pmi}
The mixed-integer problem \pmi\ adds a cardinality limit $K$ and a minimum position $\ell=\MinPositionPct\%$, moves the risk row into the objective at $\lambda^*$, and raises the position cap to $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\max\ & \alpha\T w-\lambda^*\big(y\T Fy+\textstyle\sum_i d_iw_i^2\big)\\
& \quad -c\,1\T w^- -\kappa\,1\T(w^++w^-)\\
\text{s.t.}\ & \text{the mandate of \eqref{eq:prb} without the risk row},\\
& \ell z_i^\pm\le w_i^\pm\le u_iz_i^\pm,\ z_i^++z_i^-\le1,\ \textstyle\sum_i(z_i^++z_i^-)\le K,\\
& z^\pm\in\{0,1\}^N .
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:pmi}
\end{equation}
$\lambda^*$ is \prb's multiplier on the same universe at the base mandate with $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$, fixed for that date and universe: a Lagrangian relaxation of the risk row, with zero gap in the convex case. \emph{Big-M} keeps $\sum_id_iw_i^2$ with $M=u_i$; the \emph{perspective} formulation replaces it by $\sum_id_iq_i$ with rotated cones $w_i^2\le q_i\zeta_i$, $q_i\ge0$, $\zeta_i=z_i^++z_i^-$; the \emph{rescaled perspective} divides every weight, row and bound by $\max_iu_i$ and writes each cone in its name's bound, $t_i=w_i/u_i$, $q_i'=q_i/u_i^2$, $t_i^2\le q_i'\zeta_i$, which leaves the feasible set and objective unchanged but changes what Gurobi's absolute tolerances act on (A9). These are the three \emph{arms} of N1--N3. With $\lambda^*$ fixed, \pmi's ex-ante volatility drifts (computed in N3 from the stored solutions): median \VolIOneMed\%/yr in I1 (\VolIOneMin--\VolIOneMax, $n=\VolIOneN$, \VolIOneAbove\ above the budget), \VolITwoMed\% in I2 (\VolITwoMin--\VolITwoMax, $n=\VolITwoN$), \VolNOneMed\% in N1 (\VolNOneMin--\VolNOneMax, $n=\VolNOneN$ per arm, \VolNOneAbove\ above), so Q2's slopes are of the risk-penalized objective. The \emph{continuous baseline}, \pmi\ with $\ell=0$ and no cardinality row, is mean-variance at $\lambda^*$: with the risk row binding it has \prb's optimizer and constraint duals at the base point (A1), but the value $A^*-\lambda^*\sigma_m^2$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Problem classes}
\prb\ is a convex quadratically constrained program (QCQP); its risk row is the second-order cone $\|(L_F\T y,\sqrt d\circ w)\|_2\le\sigma_m$ with $F=L_FL_F\T$. When $\lambda^*>0$ its optimal $w$ is unique: by A1, $w$ also maximizes the mean-variance objective at $\lambda=\lambda^*$ over the mandate, which is strictly concave in $w$ ($\Sigma\succ0$, and the costs are convex and piecewise linear in $w$); the split $w^\pm$ is then unique because $c,\kappa>0$. The big-M \pmi\ is a convex mixed-integer QP (every node relaxation a convex QP); the perspective \pmi\ is a mixed-integer second-order cone program.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Questions}
\label{sec:questions}
\textbf{Q1} (convex): at a fixed risk budget, which mandate constraints bind, what does each cost, and what determines that cost? \textbf{Q2} (integer): once a cardinality limit and a minimum position enter, how well do continuous sensitivity tools (relaxation duals, fixed-integer duals) predict the true marginal cost of a constraint? \textbf{Q3} (formulation and numerics): how do the big-M and perspective formulations compare as the mandate tightens, and how do solver tolerances interact with problem scaling?

\section{Solution Approach and Analysis}
\label{sec:approach}

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Experiments}
Table~\ref{tab:experiments} defines the experiments: C1--C2 answer Q1, I1--I2 Q2, N1--N3 Q3. D12 is \NDTwelve\ month-ends (\DTwelve) spanning calm and stressed markets. C1's \IdealN\ idealized solves are two mandates $\times$ three alphas $\times$ \NDTwelve\ dates: (i) all six exposures zero, (ii) the same plus dollar neutrality, each with the risk budget only. C2 sweeps one family at a time, the others at base, over (off first): \CTwoGrids. $N$ counts names (top $N$ by ADV); $K=\mathrm{round}(fS)$, half up, $S$ the support size of \prb\ at $u=\MiqpPositionPct\%$. A rule fixed in the design pilot chose the \IOneNCons\ I1 bounds: among the families with the largest median C1 elasticity at the I1 dates ($u$ and $\theta$ excluded: they set the big-M constants) and the Mom bound at \MomBound, those certified binding (A8) at $f=\Fb$ on \DIb.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Algorithms}
\prb\ is solved as the mean-variance QP $\max\,\alpha\T w-\lambda w\T\Sigma w-\text{costs}$ by Gurobi's dual simplex (tolerances \QPTol: a basic solution, its active set and duals exact up to them), with $\lambda$ root-found by Brent's method on $\log\lambda$ until volatility meets the budget to relative \RootRtol\ (A1). Clarabel's primal--dual interior-point method \cite{goulart2024clarabel} (tolerances \ClarabelTol) solves the cone form of \eqref{eq:prb} as a cross-check and the perspective relaxation of \eqref{eq:pmi} ($z\in[0,1]$), whose finite differences give its slope; dual simplex solves the big-M relaxation and the fixed-integer QP (\pmi\ with $z$ fixed at the incumbent). \emph{Plain relaxations} are the $z\in[0,1]$ relaxations solved outside the MIP, without its presolve or root cuts. Gurobi's branch and bound \cite{gurobi2026manual} stops when the relative gap is below \emph{MIPGap} (\IOneMipGap\ in I1, I2; \NOneMipGap\ in N1, N2(a)) or its \emph{Work}, a deterministic effort count, reaches $W^*=\WStar$ (\IOneWorkFactor$W^*$ in I1, I2), the Work of \WStarSeconds~s at the pilot's median \WorkRateMed\ units/s, to two significant figures; MIQCPMethod (cone handling at the nodes) stays at its default. The objective is multiplied by $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObj$, the power of ten that brings the pilot's proxies for $|U^*|$ (the mean-variance value at $\lambda^*$ on each I1 and N1 universe) to \SObjProxyMin--\SObjProxyMax; values are reported unscaled. The incumbent is \emph{polished}: the fixed-integer QP at its $z$, re-solved at tolerances \PolishTol, gives $V$. N2(b) runs Gurobi's barrier and CVXPY's \cite{diamond2016cvxpy} Clarabel and SCS (ECOS is not installed) at default tolerances against Clarabel at \NTwoRefTol.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Analysis}
\textbf{A1 (risk budget and mean-variance).} Dualizing only the risk row, with multiplier $\lambda\ge0$, gives the partial Lagrangian $\alpha\T w-\text{costs}-\lambda(w\T\Sigma w-\sigma_m^2)$; maximizing it over the mandate is mean-variance at $\lambda$. For $\lambda>0$ its maximizer $w(\lambda)$ is unique ($\Sigma\succ0$), with volatility continuous, nonincreasing in $\lambda$ and tending to 0 as $\lambda\to\infty$ ($w=0$ is feasible), so if the volatility at $\lambda_{\min}=\LambdaMin$ exceeds the budget a root $\lambda^*$ exists. There the risk row is tight (primal feasibility, complementary slackness), so $w(\lambda^*)$ satisfies the KKT conditions, which suffice for this convex program: it solves \prb\ with multiplier $\lambda^*$. Slater's condition holds ($w=0$ strictly satisfies the risk row; the other rows are affine), so strong duality holds and, conversely, every \prb\ optimum maximizes the Lagrangian at $\lambda^*$ (used in Sec.~II-F). Otherwise $\lambda^*\le\lambda_{\min}$ (the budget is treated as slack) and the solver returns $w(\lambda_{\min})$, feasible and with net alpha within $\lambda_{\min}\sigma_m^2=\SlackValueBound$ of \prb's optimum (\CSlack\ of \CNPoints\ C1 base solves, all $\alpha_\parallel$).

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A2--A3 (equality case).} With only the rows $Aw=0$ ($A$ of full row rank), no costs and no other rows, stationarity gives $w^*=\Sigma^{-1}g/(2\lambda)$ with $g=\alpha-A\T\nu$; $Aw^*=0$ gives $\nu=(A\Sigma^{-1}A\T)^{-1}A\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$. If $g\ne0$ ($\alpha\notin\mathrm{range}(A\T)$) the risk row binds, so $\lambda=\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}/(2\sigma_m)$ and $A^*_{\mathrm{eq}}=\alpha\T w^*=g\T w^*=\sigma_m\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g}$ ($\nu\T Aw^*=0$). Divided by the unconstrained $\sigma_m\sqrt{\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$, the retained fraction $\sqrt{g\T\Sigma^{-1}g/\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha}$ equals TC at $w^*$, and it is at most one by Cauchy--Schwarz in the $\Sigma^{-1}$ metric ($g\T\Sigma^{-1}g=g\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha$, as $A\Sigma^{-1}g=0$), since $g$ is the $\Sigma^{-1}$-orthogonal projection of $\alpha$ onto $\{v:A\Sigma^{-1}v=0\}$ along $\mathrm{range}(A\T)$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A4 (alignment).} Let $B$ have full column rank. $B\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ (the regression residual) gives $\Sigma D^{-1}\alpha_\perp=(D+BFB\T)D^{-1}\alpha_\perp=\alpha_\perp$, so $\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=D^{-1}\alpha_\perp$ and $B\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$, with no assumption on $F$: under the risk budget alone $\alpha_\perp$'s optimum, proportional to $\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp$, has zero factor exposure, and factor bounds $b_k>0$ have zero shadow price. With $A=B\T$, $g=\alpha_\perp$: the projection of A2 is unique, and $\alpha_\perp$ satisfies both $B\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\perp=0$ and $\alpha-\alpha_\perp=\alpha_\parallel=B\gamma\in\mathrm{range}(B)$ ($\gamma$ the regression coefficients). The cross term $\alpha_\perp\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$ vanishes, so $\alpha\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha=\alpha_\perp\T D^{-1}\alpha_\perp+\alpha_\parallel\T\Sigma^{-1}\alpha_\parallel$, and full factor neutrality retains $\sqrt{1-\varphi(\alpha)}$ of the alpha.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A5 (envelope).} By Slater's condition (A1) strong duality holds. $A^*$ as a function of the right-hand sides is the perturbation function of a convex program, hence concave, and nondecreasing in each bound because loosening it enlarges the feasible set \cite{boyd2004convex}. Where the multipliers are unique (for example under LICQ), $dA^*/dr_k=\mu_k$, also across nondegenerate active-set changes, where $\mu_k$ has a kink but $A^*$ does not; elsewhere only one-sided slopes exist, as at a cap tie $u=\theta\,\mathrm{ADV}_i/\mathrm{AUM}$. The chain rule gives the family dual of Sec.~II-D.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A6 (perspective tightness).} Over the same $(w,z)$, restricted by the same linking rows, $\zeta\in(0,1]$ gives $q\ge w^2/\zeta\ge w^2$ (and $w=0$ at $\zeta=0$), so with $\lambda^*\ge0$ the perspective relaxation's risk term is at least big-M's and its value at most big-M's.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A7 (one-asset toy).} For $\max\,aw-\lambda dw^2$ ($\lambda d>0$) over $w\in\{0\}\cup[\ell,u]$, $w\le b$, the value is 0 for $b<\ell$ and jumps at $b=\ell$ by $\max(0,a\ell-\lambda d\ell^2)$, positive iff $a>\lambda d\ell$. Below $\ell$ the true local slope is 0, and so is the fixed-integer dual. For $b<\ell$ the big-M relaxation's slope is $a-2\lambda db$ if $b<w^\circ=a/(2\lambda d)$ and 0 otherwise; the perspective relaxation's ($q$ minimized at $z=w/\ell$, so $q=\ell w$) is $a-\lambda d\ell$ if $a>\lambda d\ell$ and 0 otherwise. For $\ell/2<b<\ell$, $a-2\lambda db<a-\lambda d\ell$: where both are positive, big-M's slope is the closer to 0 although the perspective bound is the tighter. A tighter bound need not give a better slope.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A8 (integer value functions).} The \pmi\ value $U^*(b)$ is the upper envelope, over support patterns, of concave pieces: nondecreasing by feasible-set inclusion, in general neither concave nor continuous. The relaxation dual is the slope of an upper-bounding concave function, the fixed-integer dual the slope of the active piece, and a re-solve gives a secant across pieces. With $V$ the polished value, $\Ub$ Gurobi's final bound and $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}=\max(\Ub,V)+\BeffSlack|V|$, $V\le U^*\le\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at $b\pm\delta$ ($\delta$ absolute here, a percentage of $b$ in the experiments) gives the certified interval
\begin{equation}
L=\frac{V_+-\Ub_{\mathrm{eff},-}}{2\delta}\le\frac{U^*_+-U^*_-}{2\delta}\le\frac{\Ub_{\mathrm{eff},+}-V_-}{2\delta}=H,
\end{equation}
with point slope $s=(V_+-V_-)/(2\delta)$. ``Certified'' is conditional on $V$'s weights being feasible (the independent checker passes them at \VerdictTol) and on Gurobi's bound being valid up to the slack, a margin, not a proof. I1 has no violation (\KTwentyThreeViol\ at \KTwentyThreePoints\ points); N2(a) at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ has a counter-case (\FalseCertGap$|V|$, Sec.~IV-C). A case is \emph{certified binding} iff $L>0$ (unlike \emph{binds}, $e_p\ge\BindTol$, in the convex problems); $H<0$ flags solver error. In I1 and I2 both formulations are solved at every point; $V$ is the larger polished value, $\Ub$ the smaller bound, and the \emph{certified gap} is $(\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}-V)/|V|$.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\textbf{A9 (scaling).} An absolute tolerance $\tau$ on a quantity of size $m$ is a relative error $\tau/m$; rescaling a row or the objective changes the effective tolerances of an equivalent problem. At an optimum with $\lambda^*>0$ a held name has $q_i=w_i^2\in[\ell^2,u_i^2]$ ($q_i$ is minimized, not bounded), so Gurobi's absolute feasibility tolerance \GurobiFeasTol\ is a relative error of up to $\GurobiFeasTol/\ell^2=\ConeTolUnscaled$ on the smallest cones, and at most $\GurobiFeasTol(u_i/\ell)^2=\ConeTolRescaled$ with each cone in its name's bound. These scale a cone residual; they do not bound the objective error. They account for the incumbents' cone violation, with objective effect $\lambda^*\sum_id_i\max(0,w_i^2/\zeta_i-q_i)$ reported relative to $|V|$, and for certified gaps above MIPGap: the default-scaling N2(a) solves at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObj$ ended OPTIMAL (\NTwoDefScaledOpt\ of \NTwoDefScaledN), not at the WorkLimit, so their gap comes from the cone effect (Sec.~IV-C). They do not account for the default-scaling root bound, which N3 traces to Gurobi's outer approximation stopping before it converges.

% drafted-by-agent
% verify-by-hand
\subsection{Finite differences and noise}
The perspective relaxation's slope at $b$ is the central difference $\hat s=(R(b+\delta_r)-R(b-\delta_r))/(2\delta_r)$, $\delta_r=\PerspFdStep\,b$, of its values $R$: the objective at Clarabel's $(w,\zeta)$ with each $q_i$ set to $w_i^2/\zeta_i$ (0 where $w_i=0$), so every cone holds exactly. A relaxation fails if its residuals exceed \RelaxResidual\ or its duality gap exceeds $\varepsilon=\RelaxGap\max(|R|,|R_{\mathrm{ref}}|)$, $R_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the value at the unperturbed bound. If every stencil value is within $\varepsilon$ of exact, noise moves $\hat s$ by at most $\eta=\varepsilon/\delta_r$; the gap test does not prove this premise, so $\eta$ is a noise scale. The one-sided slopes $s_+=(-3R_0+4R_1-R_2)/(2\delta_r)$ and $s_-=(3R_0-4R_{-1}+R_{-2})/(2\delta_r)$, $R_j=R(b+j\delta_r)$, are recorded; $s_+-s_-$ has absolute coefficients summing to 16 over $2\delta_r$, so under the same premise noise moves it by at most $8\eta$, and a case is flagged as a kink if $|s_+-s_-|>\max(\SlopeKinkTol|\hat s|,\SlopeKinkNoise\eta)$. A relaxation's \emph{gap} at $b$ is $(R-V)/|V|$.

% drafted-by-agent
\subsection{Validation}
\TestsPassed\ passing tests and logged checks with negative controls confirm the analysis: the QP and the Clarabel QCQP agree on $A^*$ to \KFourA\ and on $\lambda^*$ to \KFourLam\ (A1); A2--A3 hold to \KSixA, the A4 split to \KFiveSplit; on \KNineToys\ one-asset toys (K29c's \KTwentyNineCToys\ random ones among them) both formulations match A7 at \KNinePoints\ grid points to \KNineErr\ (\KNineBand\ points within Gurobi's tolerance below $\ell$ excluded); \pmi\ with $K\ge N$, $\ell=0$ reproduces \prb's weights and $A^*$ to \KThirteen\ (largest relative error, in the weights). An independent feasibility checker passes every C1 and C2 solution and every polished $V$. The slope method was \emph{gated} (a pass/fail check fixed in advance) before I1, on the random toys (\KTwentyNineCMisses\ misses at \KTwentyNineCPoints\ points: each grid point $b>0$, $\ell$ and $w^\circ$; \KTwentyNineCToyFailed\ failed relaxation excluded) and \KTwentyNineCPairs\ objective-scale pairs (\KTwentyNineCPairMisses\ misses). At \KTwentyNineBScale$s_{\mathrm{obj}}$ the I1 perspective slopes meet CHECKS K29b's tolerance at \SlopeScaleWithin\ of \SlopeScaleN\ cases (the \KTwentyNineBN\ at \DIa\ as an acceptance check, the rest afterwards), moving at most \SlopeScaleBindDiff\ relative where certified binding ($n=\SlopeScaleBindN$); none of the \PerspRelax\ I1 relaxations failed.

\section{Results}
\label{sec:results}

\subsection{Q1: Constraint Costs in the Convex Problem}
\label{sec:results-q1}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} C1 and C2 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) at the D12 dates on all eligible names; the criterion is the elasticity $e_p$ from exact duals, validated as derivatives below; statistics are over D12 for $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ ($n=\NDTwelve$) unless stated.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Which constraints bind.} At base, $A^*$ has median \AMomMedBp\ bp/month (range \AMomMinBp--\AMomMaxBp), a median \RetMomMed\ (\RetMomMin--\RetMomMax) of the unconstrained, costless optimum. The risk budget binds in all but \CSlack\ of the \CNPoints\ base solves, all of them $\alpha_\parallel$. The liquidity cap binds at all \ELiqBind\ dates (median elasticity \ELiqMed), sector bounds at \ESectorBind\ (\ESectorMed), dollar neutrality at \EDollarBind\ (\EDollarMed), style bounds at \EStyleBind\ and the position cap at \EPosBind; beta and gross bind at none. At the tightest grid points (Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves}) the pod keeps a median \CTwoLiqTight\ of its alpha at $\theta=\LiqTightPct\%$ (range \CTwoLiqTightMin--\CTwoLiqTightMax), \CTwoSectorTight\ under exact sector neutrality, \CTwoStyleTight\ with every style exposure at zero and \CTwoMomTight\ with the Mom exposure alone at zero; each other family keeps at least \CTwoGrossTight, the lowest being gross at $G=\GrossTight$.

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig1_cost_curves_row.pdf}
\caption{Cost curves (C2): off = family removed, others at base (dotted: base); $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ median and interquartile band over D12; all styles also $\alpha_\perp$, $\alpha_\parallel$.}
\label{fig:costcurves}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{What determines the cost.} Factor bounds are cheap because $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ is weakly aligned with the factors: $\varphi$ is \PhiMomMin--\PhiMomMax\ over D12, and under idealized full factor neutrality the retained fraction is $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ (A4), at least \IdealRetMomMin\ (Fig.~\ref{fig:alignment}). Over the \IdealN\ idealized solves, numerical and closed-form $A^*$ agree to \IdealARelErr\ relative where the closed form is nonzero ($n=\IdealNonzeroN$) and to \IdealZeroAbs\ absolute at the \IdealZeroN\ $\alpha_\parallel$ solves where it is zero; under mandate (i) ($n=\IdealFactorN$) the fractions agree with $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ to \IdealRetErrNonPar, except for $\alpha_\parallel$, whose $\varphi$ rounds to within \IdealPhiRound\ of 1, which $\sqrt{1-\varphi}$ magnifies to \IdealRetErr. $\alpha_\perp$ ($\varphi\le\PhiPerpMax$) loses nothing and $\alpha_\parallel$ ($\varphi=\PhiParMax$) everything. At the base mandate the $\alpha_{\mathrm{mom}}$ points lie well below the curve: the cost comes from the caps and the costs. Of the base portfolio's gross expected alpha $\alpha\T w^*$, the pod keeps a median \SplitAMed\ (\SplitAMin--\SplitAMax) as $A^*$, pays \SplitTradeMed\ (\SplitTradeMin--\SplitTradeMax) in trading and \SplitBorrowMed\ (\SplitBorrowMin--\SplitBorrowMax) in borrow.

\begin{figure}[!t]

\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig2_alignment.pdf}
\caption{Retained fraction against $\varphi$ (C1), relative to the unconstrained, costless \prb; filled: mandate (i), no costs; hollow: base.}
\label{fig:alignment}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Duals as derivatives.} At every binding key and D12 date (\KFifteenN\ checks over \KFifteenKeys\ keys: the binding families, every sector, and the CMA and Mom rows) the dual matches the central difference within \KinkPct\% (largest error \KFifteenMaxErr) at $\delta=\EnvStepPct\%$ of the bound, or at $\EnvFineStepPct\%$ at the \KFifteenFlag\ flagged stencils (the dual zero at an end, or forward and backward differences more than \KinkPct\% of the central one apart; \KinkAS\ change the active set, \KinkCurv\ are curvature flags); along all \KSeventeenSweeps\ C2 sweeps $A^*$ is nondecreasing and concave in the bound (\KSeventeenFail\ failures), as A5 predicts.

\subsection{Q2: Sensitivity under Integrality}
\label{sec:results-q2}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} I1 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) perturbs \IOneNCons\ bounds by $\delta$ (sector and dollar at \BaseSectorPct\%, all styles at \BaseStyle, the Mom bound at \MomBound): \IOneCases\ cases, \IOneCasesTen\ at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$. The estimators are the big-M relaxation dual, the perspective relaxation slope and the fixed-integer dual; the baseline (Sec.~II-E) is the convex reference. The criterion is $|\hat\mu-s|/|s|$ over certified-binding cases, and whether $\hat\mu\in[L,H]$.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Certification.} No interval is violated (\KTwentyThreeViol\ of \KTwentyThreePoints\ points) and the formulations' polished values tie at all \VTieIOne. At $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, \IOneBindTen\ of \IOneCasesTen\ cases are certified binding (sector \IOneBindSector, momentum \IOneBindMom, dollar \IOneBindDollar, all styles \IOneBindStyle); in the others every estimator is zero (the perspective slope to within \NonBindPerspMax). The median relative width $(H-L)/s$ is \WidthMed\ (\WidthMin--\WidthMax, $n=\WidthN$): lying in $[L,H]$ means matching the secant to that width.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Estimator errors.} Table~\ref{tab:i1} gives the errors at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ ($n=\IOneBindTen$). The perspective slope has the smallest median error, \ErrPerspMed\ (max \ErrPerspMax), then the fixed-integer dual, \ErrFixedMed\ (max \ErrFixedMax), and the big-M dual, \ErrBigMMed\ (max \ErrBigMMax). Only \ErrFixedInLH\ estimates, all fixed-integer duals, lie in $[L,H]$. The baseline row counts the \BaseSecN\ cases where the baseline's own constraint binds ($e_p\ge\BindTol$): the \IOneBindTen\ certified-binding cases and \BaseOnlyBind\ more. Its dual is within a median \BaseSecMed\ (max \BaseSecMax) of its own secant, so integrality, not the step, causes the errors. The errors depend on $\delta$: at \IOneRobustDate\ ($n=\RobustN$ binding at each step) the medians at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ and \IOneDeltaPct\% are \RobustFixedFive\ and \RobustFixedTen\ (fixed-integer), \RobustPerspFive\ and \RobustPerspTen\ (perspective), \RobustBigMFive\ and \RobustBigMTen\ (big-M).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{When the fixed-integer dual is exact.} Each case is classed by comparing, at $b-\delta$, $b$ and $b+\delta$, the signed support of $V$'s incumbent and the fixed-integer QP's active set: P1, both unchanged; P2, support unchanged, active set changed; P3, support changed. Of the certified-binding cases, \SupPOneTen, \SupPTwoTen\ and \SupPThreeTen\ of \IOneBindTen\ are P1, P2 and P3 at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$, and \SupPOneFive, \SupPTwoFive\ and \SupPThreeFive\ of \SupBindFive\ at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$. With fixed support and active set the QP solution is affine in $b$, so the value is quadratic and the central secant is the derivative at $b$. Over both steps, the fixed-integer error is at most \PredOneMax\ in P1 ($n=\PredOneN$), within the relative \PredOneTol\ predicted before the analysis ran, at most \PredTwoMax\ in P2 ($n=\PredTwoN$), and has median \PredThreeMed\ in P3 ($n=\PredThreeN$). The relaxation slopes fail differently: their error rises with the relaxation's gap at $b$ (Spearman rank correlation \SpearmanPersp\ for the perspective, \SpearmanBigM\ for big-M, $n=\SpearmanN$).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Value functions.} I2 sweeps the sector bound, the I1 constraint with the largest median point slope over the \NearTieInst\ I1 instances at $\delta=\IOneDeltaPct\%$ (the design rule): \NearTieSector\ per unit of weight, against \NearTieMom\ per unit of loading for the Mom bound, a comparison across units; by median elasticity the Mom bound ranks first (\NearTieElMom\ against \NearTieElSector). The \pmi\ value lies below the baseline value and is not concave: \GridCertA\ of \GridTriplesA\ grid triples at \DIb\ and \GridCertB\ of \GridTriplesB\ at \DIc\ are certified nonconcave, $V(b^{(k-1)})+V(b^{(k+1)})>2\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}(b^{(k)})$, and the support changes between \GridSupChA\ of \GridPairsA\ (\DIb) and \GridSupChB\ of \GridPairsB\ (\DIc) neighbouring grid points. At $\ITwoFracLo b$, $b$ and $\ITwoFracHi b$ ($\delta=\ITwoDeltaPct\%$, $n=\ITwoN$; Fig.~\ref{fig:valuefunctions}) the median errors are \ITwoBigMMed\ (big-M), \ITwoPerspMed\ (perspective) and \ITwoFixedMed\ (fixed-integer), none in its interval (relative width at most \ITwoWidthMax).

\subsection{Q3: Formulations and Numerics}
\label{sec:results-q3}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Setup.} N1 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) solves the \NOneCell\ instances per tightness level (loose: styles \LooseStyle, beta \LooseBeta; base; tight: \TightStyle, \TightBeta) with the three arms at MIPGap \NOneMipGap\ and WorkLimit $W^*$. The criteria are Work and the root gap after Gurobi's root cut loop, (root bound $-$ best known value)$/|$best known value$|$, the best known value being the largest polished $V$ over the instance's arms and presolve settings. Default-scaling results describe how Gurobi treats the unscaled cones (solver behaviour), not the formulation.

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Root gaps and effort.} At default presolve and base tightness the rescaled perspective has the smallest median root gap, \RootRescBase\ against big-M's \RootBigMBase\ (big-M's is smaller at tight; Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}), and the least median Work at every level (base \WorkRescBase\ against \WorkBigMBase); the default-scaling perspective is far behind (\RootDefBase; Work \WorkDefBase). No solve at default presolve stopped at the WorkLimit. The plain relaxations order as A6 predicts on every instance (\KTwentyFourViol\ violations; median margin \KTwentyFourMed\ of $|V|$), with median plain gaps \PlainBigMBase\ (big-M) and \PlainPerspBase\ (perspective) at base ($n=\NOneCell$). Presolve, not the formulation, closes big-M's gap: at $N=\NOneMidN$ ($n=\PreN$ per arm), presolve off raises big-M's median root gap from \PreBigMRootOn\ to \PreBigMRootOff\ (plain: \PrePlainBigM), and \PreBigMCensOff\ of \PreN\ solves stop at the WorkLimit, the others using \PreBigMWorkOffOkMin--\PreBigMWorkOffOkMax\ Work; the rescaled perspective moves only from \PreRescRootOn\ to \PreRescRootOff\ (median Work \PreRescWorkOn\ to \PreRescWorkOff).

\begin{figure}[!t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{../figures/fig5_formulations.pdf}
\caption{N1 root gap against tightness, default presolve; $n=\NOneCell$ per cell; gray: median plain gaps.}
\label{fig:formulations}
\end{figure}

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Two mechanisms.} The default-scaling root bound is not the cone tolerance. N3 (Table~\ref{tab:experiments}) repeats the root of both perspective arms at every N1 instance at default presolve, as root-only runs (\emph{probes}); the default probe reproduces N1's root bound exactly at \NThreeReproDef\ of \NThreeN. Forcing outer approximation (MIQCPMethod 1; the default, $-1$, lets Gurobi choose) gives the same bound exactly at \NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN\ (rescaled: \NThreeEOneResc), consistent with Gurobi choosing outer approximation at most instances; its logs are off, so the choice itself is not recorded. A QCP node relaxation (method 0) lowers the median default-scaling root gap from \NThreeGapDef\ to \NThreeGapMZero, below the plain perspective relaxation's \NThreeGapPlain\ over the same \NThreeN\ instances, as root cuts allow (within $\NThreeETwoTol|V|$ of the plain relaxation at \NThreeETwoWithin), whereas the default's root bound is looser than the plain relaxation itself. FeasibilityTol \NThreeFeasTol\ leaves it at \NThreeGapFeas: the ratio of the two gaps has median \NThreeRatioMed, within a factor \NThreeBandHi\ at \NThreeRatioIn\ of \NThreeN\ instances, \NThreeCollapsed\ below, \NThreeRatioAbove\ above (max \NThreeRatioMax). The rescaled arm's gaps under the three methods stay within a factor \NThreeRescSpread\ of each other. N3 was added after the other experiments had been analysed, to test on all \NThreeN\ instances what the design pilot (S2d) had found on a subset of them. The incumbent mechanism is the cone tolerance (A9): at default presolve ($n=\ConeN$ per arm) the default-scaling incumbents violate their cones within tolerance with an objective effect of median \ConeDefMed\ and max \ConeDefMax\ of $|V|$, at most \ConeRescMax\ rescaled. The rescaled arm changes both the rows' scale (divided by $\max_iu_i$) and the cones' scale, so N1 does not separate the two. Every arm's polished value lies within every other arm's $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (\KTwentyTwoFail\ failures in \KTwentyTwoPairs\ pairs).

% drafted-by-agent
\emph{Objective scaling.} N2(a) repeats N1's base instances at $N=\NOneMidN$ at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ and \SObj. At $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ big-M stops at the WorkLimit in \NTwoBigMWLOne\ of \NTwoArmN\ instances (the others use \NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMin--\NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMax\ Work), and the rescaled perspective at \DIb\ with $K=\FalseCertK$ reported a closed gap while its $\Ub_{\mathrm{eff}}$ lay \FalseCertGap$|V|$ below big-M's polished value, a false certificate. At \SObj\ no incumbent exceeds another arm's bound (\NTwoBeatsScaled, against \NTwoBeatsOne), and the default-scaling arm's median certified gap is \NTwoDefGapScaled, above MIPGap \NTwoMipGap: its cone effect reaches \NTwoDefConeMax\ of $|V|$, while the rescaled arm's median gap is \NTwoRescGapScaled. In N2(b), \prb\ at \NTwoConvexDates, scaling the objective by \NTwoConvexScale\ cuts Gurobi's barrier errors relative to the reference, worst over the dates and both risk-row normalizations ($n=\NTwoBarrierN$ each), from \BarrierRawA\ to \BarrierScaledA\ in $A^*$ and from \BarrierRawDual\ to \BarrierScaledDual\ in the binding duals, while risk-row normalization (the risk cone divided by $\sigma_m$, to a unit right-hand side) leaves its $A^*$ identical (\BarrierNormSame\ of \BarrierNormPairs).

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\begin{outline}{V, 0.8 page; the coverage list of modeling choices, limitations, trade-offs, unexpected behavior and extensions}
\item Modeling choice, fixed risk budget against fixed $\lambda$: costs at equal risk; mean-variance recovered at $\lambda^*$ (A1) $\rightarrow$ \KFourLam.
\item Modeling choice, $\lambda^*$ fixed within (date, $N$) for \pmi: exact only without integers; the MIQP's volatility falls below the budget (I1 median \VolIOneMed\%, all \VolIOneBaseBelow\ of \VolIOneBaseN\ base points below; N1 \VolNOneAbove\ of \VolNOneN\ above), so the Q2 slopes are of the penalized objective $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:setting}, the baseline at \VolBaseIOneAt\ of \VolBaseIOneN\ I1 base points on the budget.
\item Modeling choices: single period with $w_0=0$; the six-factor, \RiskWindow-day risk model with the residual floor; the momentum construction and winsorization; the base mandate values; the \MiqpPositionPct\% cap and $\ell$ in \pmi; costs as assumptions $\rightarrow$ Table~\ref{tab:mandate}.
\item Limitations: the disclosures below.
\item Trade-off, alpha against exposure: the cost curves $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:costcurves}, \CTwoLiqTight, \CTwoSectorTight.
\item Trade-off, formulation strength against per-node cost: tighter at the root, but cone nodes $\rightarrow$ \KTwentyFourMed; median nodes at base \NodesBigMBase\ (big-M), \NodesRescBase\ (rescaled), \NodesDefBase\ (default).
\item Trade-off, tightness against effort $\rightarrow$ Fig.~\ref{fig:formulations}, \WorkBigMTight, \WorkRescTight.
\item Trade-off, tolerance against runtime: MIPGap \IOneMipGap\ (I1) against \NOneMipGap\ (N1); at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ big-M stops at the WorkLimit in \NTwoBigMWLOne\ of \NTwoArmN\ (others \NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMin--\NTwoBigMWorkOneOkMax\ Work) $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q3}.
\item What each estimator measures (A8), and why the errors depend on $\delta$ $\rightarrow$ \RobustPerspFive\ against \RobustPerspTen\ at \IOneRobustDate; at $\delta=\IOneRobustDeltaPct\%$ the P1 maxima are \ClassPerspPOneFiveMax\ (perspective) and \ClassBigMPOneFiveMax\ (big-M), $n=\ClassPOneFiveN$.
\item Two failure modes: a support change within the step for the fixed-integer dual (P3 \PredThreeMed; P1 \PredOneMax), and relaxation looseness for the relaxation slopes (Spearman \SpearmanPersp, \SpearmanBigM; perspective per class \ClassPerspPOne, \ClassPerspPThree) $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q2}.
\item The I2 near-tie: median secant \NearTieSector\ (sector, per unit of weight) against \NearTieMom\ (momentum, per unit of loading), a comparison across units; by elasticity the Mom bound ranks first (\NearTieElMom\ against \NearTieElSector); under the perspective slope the order flips, \NearTiePerspSector\ against \NearTiePerspMom\ $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:results-q2}.
\item Unexpected: presolve does big-M's root work $\rightarrow$ \PreBigMRootOn\ against \PreBigMRootOff; \PreBigMCensOff\ of \PreN\ stopped at the WorkLimit with presolve off.
\item Unexpected: the default-scaling root bound is consistent with outer approximation stopping early, not the cone tolerance $\rightarrow$ \NThreeEOneDef\ of \NThreeN, \NThreeGapMZero, \NThreeRatioMed.
\item Unexpected: the false certificate at $s_{\mathrm{obj}}=\SObjUnit$ $\rightarrow$ \FalseCertGap.
\item Unexpected: the risk-row normalization is absorbed by presolve (supported, not proven) $\rightarrow$ \ProbeSameDefault\ of \ProbeN, \ProbePresolveMax.
\item Unexpected: the hedged legs (in \HedgedRelax\ of \HedgedRelaxN\ perspective relaxations the relaxation splits a name into a long and a short leg to cheapen its cone; \HedgedNames\ name--relaxation pairs, \HedgedDistinct\ distinct names, the prediction holding at \HedgedHolds); per-leg cones as an extension $\rightarrow$ \HedgedNames, \HedgedDistinct, \HedgedHolds\ (not yet in Results).
\item Slope accuracy holds on every I1 case, not only the gated ones $\rightarrow$ \ExtWithin\ of \ExtN.
\item The earlier iteration's lessons in one or two sentences, without numbers: the fixed-risk formulation and the scaling policy.
\item Extensions: platform coordination by exposure prices (decomposition); multi-period rebalancing (MPC); robust alpha (SOCP); a Lagrangian bound for the cardinality row.
\end{outline}

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}
\begin{outline}{VI, 0.2 page}
\item Q1: neutrality is cheap for a weakly aligned alpha; the liquidity cap, sector bounds and trading costs carry the cost $\rightarrow$ \ELiqMed, \SplitTradeMed, \IdealRetMomMin.
\item Q2: the fixed-integer dual is exact on a stable support and the best estimator depends on the step $\rightarrow$ \PredOneMax, \PredThreeMed, Table~\ref{tab:i1}.
\item Q3: two mechanisms, outer approximation at the root (inferred) and the cone tolerance at the incumbent; the perspective formulation helps only in the rescaled formulation (rows and cones together), and objective scaling is still needed $\rightarrow$ \RootRescBase, \RootDefBase, \NThreeEOneDef, \FalseCertGap.
\item Extensions $\rightarrow$ Sec.~\ref{sec:discussion}.
\end{outline}
